item.title: What happens if the Liberals drop out of the Swedish parliament?
item.description: Sweden’s Liberal Party are currently below 1.5 percent in the polls, the worst result ever for an established party and well below the four percent threshold needed to enter the Swedish parliament. What would happen to their 16 seats if they drop out in the next election?

item.title: 'I'm in complete confusion': Indian entrepreneur faces threat of expulsion from Sweden
item.description: This week’s episode of Sweden in Focus Extra features an interview with the Skellefteå-based entrepreneur Abhi Nag Balasubramanya.

item.title: Sweden's SJ train company releases summer tickets early
item.description: You can book your Swedish summer train travel earlier than usual this year. Swedish state rail company SJ, which normally releases summer tickets in March or April, has this year released them on January 28th.

item.title: Sweden moves to simplify residency permits for international researchers
item.description: Sweden's government is pushing ahead with long-delayed reforms which will among other things allow PhD researchers to get permanent residency in Sweden after just three years.

item.title: How to find a job in Sweden: Five tips from those who've been there, done that
item.description: The Swedish job market poses unique challenges for newcomers. The Local's readers share their best tips for cracking the career code.

item.title: How to lower the monthly cost of your Swedish mortgage
item.description: The mortgage makes up the biggest chunk of a lot of home owners' monthly bills. But did you know there’s a way you can lower your mortgage cost?

item.title: Swedish word of the day: passa på
item.description: How do an understated people "seize the day"?

item.title: Swedish government to ban mobile phones in primary schools
item.description: Sweden's government is pushing ahead with a plan to ban students using mobile phones at all primary schools from the start of the autumn semester. The ban will also apply to breaks, after-school care, and recreation activities.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Thursday
item.description: Almost half of shop owners victims of crime last year, majority of Swedes want politicians to tackle climate change, more than usual sought help at Christmas and more news from Sweden on Thursday.

item.title: Most Swedes want government action on climate change
item.description: A WWF survey released on January 29th shows that an increasing number of Swedes think that responsibility for addressing climate and environmental issues lies with governments, not individuals.
